name: Shelter decision triggers
description: Define when the household stays put instead of evacuating.
notes: Examples: unsafe roads, official shelter guidance, short outage, hazardous outdoor conditions.

name: Shelter area
description: Choose the safest interior area or room for severe weather, unrest, smoke, or other hazards.
notes: Consider windows, flooding risk, temperature, ventilation, and accessibility.

name: Water reserve timeline
description: Track drinking, cooking, sanitation, and pet water by expected duration.
notes: Update remaining days of water each check-in period.

name: Food reserve timeline
description: Track shelf-stable food, special diets, infant needs, and cooking requirements by expected duration.

name: Sanitation plan
description: Prepare toilet, waste, handwashing, hygiene, diapers, and cleaning supplies.
notes: Include sealed trash, gloves, wipes, and backup toilet options.

name: Power conservation plan
description: Decide what stays powered, when to charge devices, and how to rotate batteries or solar.
notes: Prioritize medical devices, phones, radios, lights, hub, and battery banks.

name: Generator and fuel safety
description: Document safe generator placement, carbon monoxide precautions, fuel handling, and refueling rules.
notes: Never operate generator indoors or near open windows.

name: Medical monitoring
description: Set a cadence for medications, medical device batteries, mobility needs, and health checks.
notes: Share only necessary information with wider groups.

name: Security and safety watch
description: Define basic household safety routines without creating panic or exposing sensitive details.
notes: Include locks, lighting, smoke/CO alarms, and safe movement around the home.

name: Communications schedule
description: Choose when the household sends routine check-ins and when to escalate if no one responds.
notes: Include battery-saving windows and quiet hours.

name: Air quality and ventilation
description: Prepare filters, masks, sealed room options, and ventilation rules for smoke, dust, heat, or cold.
notes: Include HVAC/filter settings and backup masks.

name: Dependent and pet care cadence
description: Set routine checks for children, elderly household members, people with special needs, and pets.
notes: Include feeding, meds, mobility, bathroom, comfort, and sleep needs.

name: Supply status update
description: Send a concise status update when water, food, power, medical, mobility, or communications degrade.
notes: Use yellow/red Action Message states when appropriate.

name: All-clear criteria
description: Define who can declare shelter-in-place complete and what must be checked before normal activity resumes.
notes: Include home damage check and safe route check.
